title: Unified Cross-Platform Inventory Logic
business: A retail logistics firm managing inventory across mobile Android devices and web-based warehouse management systems.
problem: The firm suffers from inconsistent stock calculation logic because separate teams maintain Java-based Android apps and JavaScript-based web services, leading to frequent inventory discrepancies.
solution: Kotlin Multiplatform allows the team to consolidate core inventory calculation logic into a single shared module that compiles to both JVM bytecode for the backend and native code for mobile clients, ensuring identical business rules.
steps: Define the core inventory calculation logic within a shared Kotlin Multiplatform module.
Configure the build system to target both the JVM for the backend service and native targets for mobile.
Expose the shared business logic as a library dependency for both the Android application and the web backend.
Implement platform-specific UI layers that invoke the shared logic for data processing.
outcome: The firm achieves a single source of truth for inventory math, eliminating logic drift and reducing the time required to update stock calculation rules across all platforms.
limitation: The primary tradeoff is the increased complexity of the build configuration and the need to manage platform-specific dependencies, which can be verified by inspecting the build output logs for unexpected target-specific compilation errors.
